messages:
marina: Heads-up — customer in eu-west running a transparent outbound proxy. They can't configure an explicit proxy on our agents. Asking what IPs/ports to allow and any gotchas.
stefan: Important: transparent proxy may terminate TLS or do CONNECT tunneling. If it terminates TLS it can break mTLS and any cert-pin checks; if it does CONNECT, SNI and client certs pass through. Ask which mode they use.
jess: Quick note — our healthchecks are standard HTTPS with bearer tokens, so an MITM proxy that rewrites certs is OK for auth level, but it will break cert-based auth. Also beware of response body size limits if proxy inspects payloads.
ryan: Network thing: if their proxy/SNAT pool is small, we see ephemeral port exhaustion during high QPS bursts (batching from GPUs). Recommend >= 16384 ephemeral ports for large fleets. Also recommend preserving source port when possible (some LB modes break that).
priyanka: For allowlist we'll provide CIDRs and a short-policy. Example safe destination CIDRs: 34.72.128.0/20, 34.72.144.0/20, 34.73.0.0/18 (these are examples — pick region-specific list we'll send). Destination ports: 443 (HTTPS), 80 (HTTP for redirects/updates), 53 UDP/TCP for DNS. Also permit outbound TCP/443 to our healthcheck IPs: 34.73.10.5, 34.73.10.6.
marina: They also chain corporate proxies (transparent -> upstream explicit). Any special advice for SNI or CONNECT passthrough?
stefan: If chaining, ensure the first hop uses `CONNECT` for 443 so SNI is preserved to the upstream endpoint. If the first proxy terminates and re-encrypts, the upstream won't see original SNI. Prefer tunnel mode.
jess: Practical snippet for transparent redirect that avoids capturing probes and box-local services (example):
```
# redirect all outbound 443 to squid proxy except kube probes and our infra user
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 443 \n  -m owner ! --uid-owner 1337 \n  -m comment --comment "avoid kube-probes" -j REDIRECT --to-ports 3129
```
marina: Also callout DNS behavior — if the proxy intercepts DNS, check that EDNS and DNS-over-TLS passthrough are supported; otherwise service discovery and SRV lookups may fail for our internal endpoints.
ryan: Logging/observability tip: they should preserve X-Forwarded-For and/or add their proxy client IP header so we can map requests to customer hosts during debugging. If proxy rewrites those headers, ask for proxy logs.
priyanka: I'll put together a short checklist we can send: 1) allow CIDRs + ports, 2) ensure NAT pool >= 16k ports, 3) use CONNECT/tunnel for TLS, 4) preserve SNI or use passthrough for mTLS, 5) keep healthcheck IPs whitelisted, 6) forward XFF.
opsbot: infra-bot: egress endpoint healthcheck (eu-west) succeeded at 2026-03-17T14:01:22Z :white_check_mark:
marina: perfect. priyanka can you draft the email and drop it in #eng-platform? I'll cc solutions. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
priyanka: on it — will include the iptables snippet, NAT sizing notes, and a small diagram of proxy chaining behavior.
